issues.detail: The Greek 'βλεπετε' (look/take note) is rendered as 'hãy coi chừng' (be careful/watch out), which carries a nuance of warning or caution that is not present in the Greek text. A more faithful rendering would be 'hãy lưu ý' or 'hãy biết rằng'.

The Greek 'αφοβως γενηται' (let him [be] fearless) is rendered as 'được không sợ hãi' (to be not afraid). While the meaning is similar, 'hãy để ông ấy [được] không sợ hãi' would better capture the imperative/exhortative mood of the Greek.
